questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I find the history of Catalonia interesting, especially the history from the spanish civil war, which introduced me to Spanish culture and general history. I also saw a movie that inspired me to go to Spain

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Somewhat easy, not that much information was needed

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was recieved by a mentor, who would show us around the school. I would maybe have liked more activities to meet more people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: When i was searching for a place, i could only pick a shared room

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: We had a kitchen, without an oven

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That it is far away from the city, about 45 min, but close to the university

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I first lived in Central Barcelona, but i moved early on to the dormitory close to UAB

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Very confusing with the courses, as i was using the online course catalogue, but it turned out to be wrong as i had to use another course catalogue, which i and a lot of other students only found out later

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Exchange Office was very helpful at fixing all the problems we had with courses

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was somewhat succesful, but i didn't manage to get the obligatory courses i needed

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To be sure to check that you are looking at the right course catalogue

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses were not very high, and we often had to take very random courses, as there was not enough space in the courses i needed to get

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: One thing that UCPH can learn better, is the higher level of interaction between students, and less lectures. So more interactive classes

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Public Policy Analysis
Cooperation in Humanitarian Development and Aid 
Public International Law
Environmental Law
European Internal Market Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: European Internal Market Law, only for nerdy law students, but it was interesting to know more about the laws regulating our market for companies in EU

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't expect to but pots and pans for myself in the dormitory

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: cheaper than expected, in terms of food

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Very cheap sport opportunities, fitness, swimming, tennis etc. for only 100 kr per month. Some social activities existed, but not that many

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Attend some of the erasmus social events and try to talk with the local people and students to learn more about their life in Catalonia

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Montserrat, Girona, go to Morocco, Tibidabo, The Gothic Quarter

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It is not that hard, but the biggest thing is the language barrier. There are also some problems with incoming students and between the local students, related to the "tourist go home" conflict, that Barcelona is experiencing

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the parties, meet them in class, go to the social events, try to learn some Catalan or Spanish, go to language cafes and bars

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language barrier is the biggest problem, when trying to befriend people

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The social energy of the Spanish people, their dances and music and their directness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: That they should be ready and open to meet people from other countries and that the university is located far away from central barcelona

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: That the housing situation is a little hard in barcelona so, it's good to be ready with that

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people i met and meeting the Spanish people. Very interesting people

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The languauge barrier and the problems with my courses and erasmus funding

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
